    Fire Sale: Here's Why Now May Be the Perfect Time to Buy Nvidia Stock

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (696 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that there are multiple reasons why Nvidia (NVDA -0.89%) is a great stock to buy right now, but investors must understand the risks, too.
    • Industry observers note that at the end of the day, I think Nvidia's stock is still trading at fire-sale prices.
    • The Nvidia turmoil has been notable lately.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Keithen Drury – Nov 27, 2026 at 9:18AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Industry observers note that there are multiple reasons why Nvidia (NVDA -0.89%) is a great stock to buy right now, but investors must understand the risks, too. Fortunately, one of those risks just went away with Jensen Huang returning to the CEO position.

    Industry observers note that at the end of the day, I think Nvidia's stock is still trading at fire-sale prices. I think now is the perfect time to swoop in and scoop up shares, as a deal this good won't last forever.

    The Nvidia turmoil has been notable lately. It all started with co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang resigning from his position after admitting being unfaithful to his wife. But then the board reinstated him a few days later. But he's not out of hot water yet, as he must appear before Congress to testify on Nvidia's chip shipments. A woman he’s alleged to have had an affair with is rumored to be a Chinese spy.

    NASDAQ · As of 10:39 AM ET 11/27/26.

    Another issue with Nvidia right now is concerns about how accurate its financials are regarding chip sales to China. The U.S. has banned the export of some types of chips. What was legally allowed to be sent directly to China was $2.4 billion for Nvidia in Q3, and it is no longer shipping these products to China.

    But what makes investors worried is how many chips were being sold to companies in other countries that were illegally diverting them to China. There are a handful of government entities that are probing Nvidia for these allegations, which could bring about fines. This comes with a risk of Nvidia potentially losing sales to some of these companies, which could affect Nvidia's total revenue.

    However, I’m not worried. If there were a massive and obvious part of Nvidia's business that was being sold internationally that didn't add up to what domestic companies were spending on AI, this would have raised red flags long ago.

    While I think there may have been some (maybe a percent or two) of sales that ended up in places that they weren't supposed to be, the majority of Nvidia's revenue base is fine, and the companies behind that revenue base look like they are going to spend more next year.

    It has been revealed that after the catastrophic sell-off, Nvidia's stock now trades for about 14 times earnings as I write this. For reference, the S&P 500 (^GSPC +1.13%) trades for about 20 times trailing earnings.

    So, even without any growth baked into the stock, Nvidia is trading at a discount to the broader stock market.

    When you factor in next year's estimated growth, this gets even more mismatched. During its Q3 conference call, then-interim CEO Colette Kress raised next year's revenue growth guidance from 70% to 75%. The reason is obvious: The AI hyperscalers are spending more and more on AI. This isn't going to change, and Nvidia's products practically sell themselves.

    When you factor in next year's potential growth, the stock trades for an unbelievable 9.3 times next year's earnings estimates.

    NVDA PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts.

    Those price tags are reserved for companies where failure is imminent or that have single-digit revenue growth. Nvidia is neither, and I think this fire sale could be one of the greatest opportunities to invest in Nvidia since the start of the AI arms race in 2023. While there will be some scary headlines that appear about Nvidia over the next few months, I think it will emerge OK, making now a perfect time to load up on shares, hold onto them for a few years, and massively profit.

    Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang

    📅 21 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 22 min read (4336 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~22 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the new Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions.
    • It has been revealed that “Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City.
    • Recent findings suggest that there will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the new Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

    It has been revealed that “Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

    Recent findings suggest that there will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

    It has been revealed that as it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

    "The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ.

    It has been revealed that there was also another promising performance by upcoming signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimarães, absent through injury for a few days, was certainly not needed here.

    Industry observers note that “They know how to do it,” Arteta said of his players. “They know what they have to do. There was a lot to like in the performance. The manner we started the game, with such domination, clarity, understanding and flow, it was really impressive. At this level the players have to be decisive. They were certainly decisive today.”.

    According to recent reports, coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

    In a recent development, “Arsenal were the best team in the league last year and they indicated it,” Lampard remarked. “They played like it. The noise here at the start of the game, it was different. I remember that noise. It’s different to the Championship.”.

    "They played like champions" 🏆Frank Lampard said Coventry will learn lessons after their 3-0 opening day defeat to Arsenal ❌ pic.twitter.com/wqA2kngUVt.

    Before this opening match, Arteta had objected to the idea that Arsenal were planning to “defend” their title. Instead, he said, they are going to “attack” the Premier League once again. It was a classic Arteta-ism, but the manager’s meaning was clear: he wants his team to be aggressive, inventive and courageous. Perhaps more so than in the second half of last season, when their defending was a greater strength than their attacking.

    If that was a case of Arteta talking the talk, then his players happily followed it up by walking the walk here. Arsenal played with an unmistakable swagger, as if they simply knew there would only be one outcome against a group of Coventry players with limited experience at this level.

    The energy of the home supporters, as buoyant as you might expect following last season’s triumph, undoubtedly helped Arsenal. There were none of the nerves that defined the run-in in the spring, with the fans instead in a partying mood from the moment fresh signing Ezri Konsa was introduced to the Emirates Stadium before kick-off.

    The opening goal took only 15 minutes to arrive, as Havertz swept in an accurate finish from Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross. It has been a good summer for Havertz, who missed so much of last season with injury but has found some rhythm over the past few months. Including friendlies and his performances for Germany at the World Cup, this was his 10th goal in his last 17 appearances.

    Industry observers note that coventry have invested in some powerful, commanding players this summer, but there were signs that the physical battle was proving difficult for Lampard’s side. Caleb Yirenkyi is their new club-record signing in midfield, but he was brutally thrown to the floor by Lewis-Skelly in the first half.

    Sources indicate that saka’s goal was the result of a quick cross by Tzolis, the latest £34m winger who has made such an exciting start to his Arsenal career. The Greek forward was the star of the first half, constantly making things happen, and his delivery was diverted into Saka’s path after 23 minutes.

    "Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh.

    Recent findings suggest that odegaard revealed in the Community Shield that he is in a more confident place than the last campaign, when he constantly battled injuries, and his early-season form continued here. His goal was scruffy, bobbled in off the right foot, but his all-round performance was typically smooth. With two goals in two games, he has already beaten his tally from last season.

    "It's a top finish I would say" 😂Martin Odegaard reacts to his goal against Coventry! pic.twitter.com/mciFfZ6Fhx.

    From there, the game was over. Arsenal could remove Saka, Rice and Odegaard, safe in the knowledge that their work was done. A comfortable night for the champions, and the perfect start.

    Industry observers note that "How are you going to keep everyone happy? Winning." 🔥Mikel Arteta reveals his secret for keeping his full squad content after Arsenal's 3-0 win against Coventry 👀 pic.twitter.com/IarLijhd6I.

    "I think we can do even better to be fair" Martin Odegaard reflects on Arsenal's win over Coventry in the first game of the season 💭 pic.twitter.com/nB2YW83VlE.

    According to recent reports, it’s all over in the capital and Arsenal have started their reign as Premier League champions with a confident and assured three-goal victory over newly-promoted Coventry. Havertz, Saka and Odegaard were all on target in a flawless team performance from Arteta’s men. It’s been a tough evening for Lampard’s side, who simply couldn’t handle Arsenal.

    Sources indicate that FULL-TIME: Arsenal cruise to victory against Coventry on the opening day of the newly introduced season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/ctybTEor9J.

    Recent findings suggest that there will be four minutes of added time to round this game off. Merino shoots from long range and aims for the bottom corner, but Rushworth dives to his left and makes the stop.

    In a recent development, awoniyi tries to make a run in behind Arsenal’s defence and latch onto Hamer’s pass. The striker is hauled to the ground by Mosquera, who is lucky to escape a booking. The resulting delivery is smacked straight out of play by Torp. That is such a disappointing cross.

    Recent findings suggest that torp swings a cross into Rudoni, who makes a run from deep. Rudoni meets the delivery, but his glancing header is straight at Raya. It’s Coventry’s best chance of the match but they’ve failed to convert it. Arsenal’s clean sheet remains intact.

    Arteta makes his fifth and final substitution as Calafiori, who recorded the assist for Arsenal’s opener, is withdrawn for Hincapie.

    Lampard responds with his own alteration, bringing Hamer on for Tchaouna.

    In a recent development, coventry are still waiting for their first shot on target this evening. Arsenal are seeing this game out with exemplary professionalism.

    Sources indicate that odegaard and Tzolis are the next players to leave the field. Eze and World Cup winner Merino are on as their replacements. Arteta’s substitutions tonight have underlined Arsenal’s tremendous squad depth, and that is without the involvement of both Guimaraes and Konsa.

    It has been revealed that lewis-Skelly tries to slide a pinpoint pass through to Calafiori, in an attempt to recreate Arsenal’s opening goal from their Community Shield triumph. It nutmegs Torp, but Rushworth makes a quick dash off his line to collect the ball and eliminate any danger.

    It has been revealed that lampard adds some fresh legs and orders a double change. Awoniyi, who makes his Coventry debut, and Rudoni are on, with Simms and Thomas-Asante taken off.

    In a recent development, here come some Arsenal changes. Rice and Saka depart to loud ovations, with Zubimendi and Madueke on to replace them.

    Tzolis motors into the Coventry penalty area once again and picks out Havertz, who makes a intelligent run across the six-yard box. Before he can cross or shoot, Thomas sprints over to make an interception.

    The visitors then fail to clear a corner and Tzolis slams a low, powerful effort at goal. Rushworth gets down low and spills it, but Thomas is there to hack it away.

    Lampard makes the first change of the match for either side as Torp replaces Yirenkyi, whose endured a difficult debut in central midfield for his new side.

    Odegaard is enjoying himself out there this evening. Just as he did against Manchester City, he’s playing with such authority, purpose and confidence.

    According to recent reports, the ball breaks to Tzolis who unleashes a venomous effort at goal. It takes a significant deflection and flies out for a corner.

    In a recent development, from a Coventry corner, Arsenal counter attack with such intensity and speed. The move ends as Odegaard attempts to find Tzolis with a through ball, but the Norwegian overhits the pass and delayed it too long. The offside flag is then raised against Tzolis.

    Van Ewijk attempts to find Simms with a chipped cross towards the back post, but it’s marginally over the striker’s head as Coventry step up their search to pull a goal back.

    Sources indicate that it’s a nightmare start to the second half for Coventry. Whatever Arteta said to his players at the break has worked wonders.

    Lewis-Skelly then shoots from long range and his shot is tipped over the bar by Rushworth.

    White overlaps Saka and latches onto the winger’s pass. Saka then tees up Odegaard, who scuffs his close-range effort. Rushworth is wrong-footed and despite getting a glove to it, the ball trickles into the net and Arsenal are cruising.

    Recent findings suggest that it's Martin Odegaard... Arsenal have three! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/LrqSSGJWE6.

    Odegaard has scored some beautiful goals in an Arsenal shirt. That wasn’t one of them. He won’t care, though. Two goals in two games for the Arsenal captain.

    Read more about his return to form here: https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/08/21/odegaard-a-man-possessed-in-bid-to-unlock-arsenal-attack/.

    We are back under way for the second half. Will Arsenal add more goals to their tally or can Coventry produce a memorable comeback?

    It’s been a steep learning curve for the newly-promoted side, who have been overpowered and outclassed by Arsenal’s quality.

    Sources indicate that arsenal are in complete control thanks to a commanding first half display against Coventry. Havertz and Saka have the goals, with the reigning Premier League champions on course to claim a routine three points to kickstart their title defence.

    In a recent development, once again, Saka plays a short corner. Odegaard then passes to Rice, who is in acres of space on the edge of the penalty area. The midfielder shoots, but his curling effort drifts narrowly wide of the far post.

    There will be two minutes of added time at the end of this half.

    The ball bobbles into Tchaouna’s path and the winger tries a very ambitious acrobatic effort from the edge of the box. It had Raya worried for a second, but the effort lands on the roof of the net. That would have been a spectacular goal if it had sneaked in.

    In a recent development, tzolis teases Thomas and works some space before clipping a cross in towards Havertz. The forward doesn’t connect with the header and Coventry scramble it clear.

    Odegaard is pulling the strings and slips a delightful pass through to the onrushing White, who finds himself very far forward, but the right back is swiftly closed down by Coventry’s defence as he shoots.

    At the other end, Simms does brilliantly to turn Gabriel and win a free kick just outside the box. The Brazilian centre back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

    According to recent reports, coventry are feeling the full effects of the stark difference in levels between Championship and Premier League. Arsenal look streets ahead at the moment.

    Christos Tzolis has only played a few games for Arsenal but it’s already easy to see why he registered 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He has shown on numerous occasions this summer that he is willing to cross the ball as soon as he receives it. No delay, no faff. It worked against Manchester City last weekend and it created Saka’s goal here.

    It has been revealed that welcome back to the Premier League, Coventry... It’s been a chastening opening 27 minutes for Lampard’s side.

    Yirenkyi then receives a yellow card on his debut for pulling Lewis-Skelly’s shirt.

    Recent findings suggest that rice strides through midfield and plays a one-two with Odegaard. The English midfielder tees up Tzolis, whose fires a cross into the corridor of uncertainty. Rushworth parries it into the danger zone, gifting an unmarked Saka a simple finish from close range. What a start for the champions!

    "Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh.

    Recent findings suggest that arsenal are purring and oozing confidence. Coventry need to be careful and must stay in this game. They cannot allow Arsenal to get a second and run away with this.

    Coventry had started well but their first error in defence was ruthlessly punished. That’s Havertz’s 10th goal in his last 17 matches for club and country (including pre-season friendlies). After such an injury-disrupted campaign last year, he’s had a very good summer.

    Van Ewijk fails to clear his lines and he’s closed down by Tzolis. The ball ricochets into Calafiori’s path and the left back picks out Havertz with a low cross.

    The German sweeps a composed shot into the bottom corner. It’s such a cultured finish and Arsenal begin their defence of the Premier League with a 1-0 lead after 15 minutes.

    "The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ.

    Some steady possession for Coventry, who are looking to take the sting and excitement out of the game while also calming the buoyant Arsenal fans down.

    Recent findings suggest that tzolis pops up on the right wing and latches onto Rice’s pass. The attacker then delivers a first-time cross into the box which finds Saka, whose half-volley is blocked by Amenda.

    Sources indicate that arsenal then work a short corner that ends with White teeing up Tzolis, but his low strike is smothered by Coventry’s defence. Tzolis has certainly made a lively start, and unsurprisingly, Arsenal’s set pieces are causing some early problems.

    Tzolis looks dangerous as he dribbles at Van Ewijk, before cutting inside and unleashing a powerful shot. However, his effort is high and wide. Nevertheless, it’s positive play from Arsenal’s new signing.

    In a recent development, following that Coventry corner, the Premier League holders have monopolised the possession in the early minutes. Chants of ‘Champions of England, we know what we are’ ring around the stadium thanks to the home support, who are in full voice.

    Coventry get us under way and the newly-promoted side have won an early corner, which is comfortably dealt with by Arsenal’s defence.

    Sources indicate that the atmosphere at the Emirates is electric. Can Arsenal flex their title-winning credentials once again or will Coventry cause an almighty upset?

    New Arsenal signing Ezri Konsa has been presented on the pitch, with both sets of players set to follow him any moment now.

    The 2026-27 season is just minutes away from kicking off.

    Coventry have recruited some powerful, aggressive players this summer. They will be looking to frustrate Arsenal by shutting down the spaces around their penalty area, and they will certainly be competitive at set-pieces.

    Meanwhile, the Arsenal fans have just had their first glimpse of Ezri Konsa in the club’s shirt. The newly introduced signing walked out onto the pitch to wave to the supporters.

    With just over five minutes until the 2026-27 Premier League season starts, here are tonight’s teams in full...

    Arsenal: Raya, White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori, Odegaard, Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.

    Subs: Arrizabalaga, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Nwaneri, Merino, Zubimendi, Dowman.

    Coventry: Rushworth, van Ewijk, Thomas, Amenda, Dasilva, Onyeka, Yirenkyi, Grimes, Thomas-Asante, Simms, Tchaouna.

    Subs: Wilson, Rudoni, Sakamoto, Awoniyi, Kitching, Latibeaudiere, Eccles, Overgaard, Hamer.

    Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “He had a slight tension in his groin. He hasn’t done a pre-season, he only had four or five days before that [Man City] game. We have to take a lot of newly introduced stuff for him as well. We need to take it bit by bit.”.

    Another game, another snub for Gabriel Martinelli. As was the case against Manchester City in last weekend’s Community Shield, the Brazilian isn’t even on the bench tonight. It’s quite clear what’s going on here: Arsenal need to make sales and he is an obvious candidate to depart. It’s not particularly pleasant, though, and you can’t help but feel for a player who has been so key to this club over the last seven years.

    It has been revealed that martinelli has made it clear he does not want to move to Galatasary, who made an offer recently. Will a more suitable club come forward for him? We’ll find out in the coming days.

    In two full seasons at Coventry between 2021 and 2023, Viktor Gyokeres scored 40 goals in 97 games for Coventry, and was part of the side that lost on penalties to Luton Town in the Championship play-off final to Luton Town.

    If Coventry had won that game, would Gyokeres still be wearing a sky blue shirt instead of joining Sporting CP and then Arsenal, who knows...

    The striker will have to wait to get onto the pitch against his former team, with Mikel Arteta choosing Kai Havertz to lead the line.

    Recent findings suggest that odegaard comes into the new Premier League season, which begins when Arsenal host Coventry City on Friday night, with a point to prove. That may sound unusual, given his new-found status as a title-winning captain, but last year was a strange one for the 27-year-old. The club’s most successful campaign of his time at Arsenal was also the most frustrating one for Odegaard as an individual.

    Last season, Arsenal clinched a much-anticipated Premier League title for the first time in 22 years and are the favourites to lift the trophy for a second successive season. Mikel Arteta’s side have recently claimed the Community Shield and look like they mean business.

    Arsenal are clearly not resting on their laurels in their bid to win another top-flight title, having strengthened their squad this summer with the signings of Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa.

    Arteta looks raring to go and ready to mount another title charge.

    "Everything has to start with me" 💪Mikel Arteta states Arsenal are ready for the fresh Premier League season 💥 pic.twitter.com/rsUcs7ot7T.

    After last season’s Championship by a whopping 95 points under Frank Lampard’s management, Coventry head into their first Premier League campaign since suffering relegation from the competition in 2001.

    Coventry were playing in the fourth tier as recently as 2017, so lining up against the Premier League holders is a full-circle moment for the club and supporters that is richly deserved.

    "I loved it, I loved driving here, feeling the atmosphere, the fans" Frank Lampard on what tonight means for him and Coventry 😍Watch live here: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/077Bga2Z4W.

    On Friday night, at the home of champions Arsenal, Coventry officially begin a upcoming chapter back in the Premier League and expectations will be high. The man responsible for that tidal wave of optimism is Lampard, their promotion hero.

    He has proved a transformative appointment since arriving in November 2024, and the former England and Chelsea captain is relishing the chance to rattle some cages.

    His return is a feel-good story and Lampard has a point to prove. He admits that the desire to upset his detractors drives him on. “I’ve got experience of the Premier League and hopefully I can get that across to the players,” he mentioned.

    “The club has been out of this division for 25 years so of course it’s exciting. We want to challenge and we want to do well. I’m pleased that we’re here and you want to work at the top. We’re very focused on the job.”.

    In a recent development, arsenal ruined Enzo Maresca’s first competitive outing as Man City’s new manager in the club’s first match without Pep Guardiola. It was one-way traffic as Arsenal cruised to a resounding 3-0 win to lift the Community Shield in Cardiff.

    Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring just 23 seconds after he was brilliantly played in by Myles Lewis-Skelly’s defence-splitting pass. Arsenal doubled their lead before the half-hour mark through Kai Havertz’s close-range header and Martin Odegaard added a sumptuously taken third shortly after the interval.

    The Premier League holders were in a ruthless mood and completely overran their opponents. Christos Tzolis grabbed two assists out on the left wing, Bruno Guimarães produced a typically commanding performance in the first half and Odegaard controlled proceedings with his creativity.

    It was an early taste of silverware for Mikel Arteta’s men, who are the overwhelming favourites to retain their Premier League crown.

    "I'm really pleased, that's a really good team" Ian Wright is happy with the Arsenal starting XI to face Coventry, do you agree? 💬 Watch live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/IUBlMS963w.

    Fresh signings Aurele Amenda, Loum Tchaouna and Caleb Yirenkyi all start and make their Coventry debuts this evening.

    Carl Rushworth and Frank Onyeka also begin from the outset after making their moves permanent following successful loans last season.

    Recent findings suggest that your City tonight. 📋 pic.twitter.com/V0nzaemLYF.

    In a recent development, as Sam Dean confirmed earlier on, Bruno Guimaraes is absent from the squad. The Brazilian was subbed off at half-time in the dominant Community Shield victory over Manchester City with a thigh matter.

    Both Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka start after being used off the bench in the Community Shield last weekend, with Guimaraes and Noni Madueke dropping to the bench.

    🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Your Premier League opening day XI ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/yRf2BEs3BA.

    To soften the blow of Bruno Guimaraes’ absence from tonight’s squad due to injury, the Premier League holders can rejoice over the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for over £50m.

    The centre back has penned a four-year deal with the option of a further year.

    Speaking to Arsenal’s official website, Sporting Director Andrea Berta remarked: “Ezri is a defender of high quality, whose athleticism, composure and tactical intelligence have established him as one of the Premier League’s most consistent performers.

    “Being comfortable in both central defence and at right-back, Ezri will bring valuable versatility to our squad while maintaining the high defensive standards which are fundamental to our challenge of winning major trophies.”.

    Konsa will play no role in tonight’s encounter, having only completed the move earlier in the day.

    Reinforcing the backline ✍️ pic.twitter.com/deYQhZcmOy.

    It has been revealed that good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

    According to recent reports, the assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without upcoming £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not presently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

    Meanwhile, Arteta has stated he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

    “In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”.

    Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

    “We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he noted. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”.

    In a recent development, this is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

    Booking momentum across leisure and business travel is accelerating into 2027. Constrained lodging supply gives DiamondRock room to raise rates, while management focuses on pricing discipline, labor efficiency, and direct booking channels to defend margins.

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By TMF Breakfast News – Nov 27, 2026 at 9:29AM EST.
    • According to recent reports, money talk often finds its way to the Thanksgiving table.
    • You don’t need a crystal ball to hold your own — just honest perspective from investors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By TMF Breakfast News – Nov 27, 2026 at 9:29AM EST.

    According to recent reports, money talk often finds its way to the Thanksgiving table. One cousin wants stock picks, an uncle is calling a crash, and someone who’s never invested wants to know where to start.

    You don’t need a crystal ball to hold your own — just honest perspective from investors. So we asked our analysts how they’d build a portfolio from scratch, what drives their investing, and when a stock gave them the ick. Bring their answers to the table.

    This one’s for the relative who just opened a brokerage account. Here’s how three analysts would start from scratch.

    If I were starting from scratch as an investor now, I would build a three-stock portfolio that offers stability, diversification, and growth. Here’s what I would go for:.

    In a recent development, as one of the more value-oriented investors on the Hidden Gems team, I have quite a few stocks in my portfolio that could be considered to be excellent “beginner” stocks. But if I had to choose just three to start a portfolio with, they would likely be Berkshire Hathaway (BRKB +0.10%), Brookfield (BN +2.01%), and Realty Income (O +0.14%).

    In reverse order, I would choose Realty Income because it’s an excellent compounder with a 30-year track record of excellent total returns, and Brookfield because it’s a great combination of reliable fee-based income and investments in some of the most promising types of real assets. Finally, Berkshire is like a well-diversified portfolio all in one stock, and I’ve noted many times that if I could only own a single publicly traded manufacturer, it would be the one.

    Each quarter, the Stock Advisor team builds our list of Foundational stocks: 10 stocks that can form the basis of a well-diversified Foolish portfolio. That exercise is essentially the same as deciding what to buy when starting from scratch. It should be no surprise then, that my answer is obvious: Amazon (AMZN +3.18%) and Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX -7.04%).

    According to recent reports, both of these businesses bring scale, leadership, and a credible path to decades-long success. They balance sector exposure and business-model risk while still putting capital toward companies with clear competitive advantages that are representative of some of the best the stock market has to offer. Two stocks do not a portfolio make, but I believe this is a strong starting point for many investors.

    We asked our analysts what’s driving their investing this year. Their answers are worth borrowing as you blueprint for 2027.

    I will soon turn 54, and while I still feel like a kid, the fact is I’m not getting any younger. While I still love finding and investing in those great growth stories, I’m also slowly moving into more of a “protect your wealth” mindset.

    It has been revealed that retirement isn’t even a word in my lexicon today; I love what I do and where I get to do it and will keep on doing it as long as the Fool will have me. But last year I set out to really focus on dividend exposure in my portfolio and 2027 is going to be another year where that remains a top priority. Rest assured I’ll be checking in on our Dividend Investor service quite frequently.

    I recently read a book called Sport’s Perfect Storm: An Industry Now Totally Adrift, by Roger Mitchell.

    This line caught my attention: “In everything, the past is always prologue.”.

    After several years dedicated almost exclusively to reading investment books, this year, I’ve concentrated my leisure reading primarily on business history, and simply history. Learning about the past will give me a better perspective when investing for the future. Plus, this newly introduced focus feels particularly timely given that this year marks the 250th anniversary of American independence.

    In a recent development, as the late Charlie Munger once noted: “There is no better teacher than history in determining the future. There are answers worth billions of dollars in a $30 history book.

    According to recent reports, I want to think through and take bigger, bolder investment decisions that will play out decades from now. I want to find the compounding decade busters! By doing the research and building the conviction, you can build the investment positions.

    However, then it takes discipline and patience to see those investments play out over the next few decades. It’s often so counterintuitive: you get super excited about something new (the dopamine hit) and then you have to wait … and wait … and wait (the sugar crash). Rome wasn’t built in a day, and neither was a truly Rule Breaking portfolio.

    In a recent development, I turned 57 this year, which puts me within a decade of retirement. I also know that many workers are forced to retire sooner than expected. So it’s probably time for me to start reducing my risk by beginning to build a bond tent that will get me through the “retirement danger zone”: a time when a bear market could delay my plans or force me to sell investments when they’re down.

    In a recent development, however, like many Motley Fool members, I much prefer investing in stocks, and see investing in cash and bonds as the equivalent of being forced to eat broccoli because it’s good for me. (I don’t like broccoli.) So I will spend this year finding the balance between being prudent and pushing the envelope.

    Someone will ask if you’ve ever gotten one wrong. Here, three analysts share the moment a stock gave them pause, and what they did next.

    According to recent reports, alphabet (GOOG -0.48%) is one of my oldest, high-conviction portfolio positions. However, there was a period where I (along with many other investors) was concerned that its core search infrastructure might be unprepared for an AI universe disrupted by ChatGPT, despite it having invented much of the transformer architecture behind modern AI.

    In a recent development, today, Alphabet is positioning Google Cloud as a primary growth engine, with an impressive backlog largely driven by enterprise AI adoption, it’s designing its own AI silicon through its custom TPUs, and is successfully integrating AI tools that keep customers within the Google ecosystem. While capex is substantial, it has the margins and cash position to maintain its trajectory without compromising a profitable growth story, and that’s a value proposition I continue to believe in.

    I first researched Pinterest (PINS +5.63%) in 2019 and was instantly enamored with the potential. The user base was smaller than other platforms, yet growing fast. And it was undermonetized. I called it an “exponential growth opportunity” because it could stack user growth on top of monetization growth.

    Sources indicate that my investment thesis for Pinterest appears broken, which is why I finally sold last year. Plenty of smart Fools think I’m wrong, and that may ultimately prove to be the case. But its most recent quarter demonstrated only 17% growth in ad impressions and a 4% drop in pricing. In my view, the platform is getting oversaturated with ads, and many advertisers still aren’t willing to pay a premium price after all these years.

    It has been revealed that I’ve long admired Oracle’s (ORCL +1.37%) specialized “RDMA” server technology that’s so well suited to handle AI workloads, and in the several quarters since I finally bought in, my shares have appreciated handsomely. It’s loaded with debt however, and I’ve looked to super extended debt maturities as a mitigating factor. However, a slate of 2025 and 2026 borrowings for data center build-outs bent my buy thesis — I felt the “ick” after some back-of-the-napkin math!

    My thesis didn’t break, due to explicit capital allocation and free cash flow assurances the organization shared at its 2026 Investor Day in late October. But I continue to train a critical eye on capital expenditures, free cash flow, and the balance sheet strength of the cloud-based tech titans I own.

    None of the analysts claim to know where the market is headed next — and that’s the point. They focus on businesses, not stocks, and make investment decisions accordingly.

    You can bring that exact discipline and mindset to Thanksgiving. If someone asks what the market will do in 2027, it’s fine to skip the guesswork. Shift the question instead and ask, which businesses they’d want to own for the next decade, and why.

    Sources indicate that that’s a conversation worth having over dessert. And for anyone just getting started, remind them that every great portfolio starts with a single first step.

    According to recent reports, from all of us at The Motley Fool, Happy Thanksgiving. Fool on!

    If a younger relative asked you over pie for one rule or piece of advice to build real wealth over the next decade, what would you tell them?

    In a recent development, viper Energy (VNOM) is a subsidiary of Diamondback and owns and acquires mineral and royalty interests, primarily in the Permian Basin. The company reported upbeat third-quarter earnings, supported by recent acquisitions and continued development activity from Diamondback and third-party operators. Viper declared a base cash dividend of 50 cents per share for Q3 2026, payable on Nov. 19. Based on the base and variable dividends announced over the past 12 months, VNOM's dividend yield stands at 5.7%.

    Following the Q3 results, TD Cowen analyst Aaron Bilkoski reiterated a buy rating on Viper Energy stock with a price target of $61. The analyst noted that the company delivered solid Q3 results, with production, including oil and natural gas liquids, exceeding both TD Cowen and consensus estimates.

    The 5-star analyst highlighted that the key enhancement was the announcement of two royalty acquisitions for $809 million in cash, including deferred consideration, and $82 million of newly issued shares.

    Given the recently confirmed base dividend hike, Bilkoski expects Viper to direct incremental free cash flow toward buybacks. While the acquisitions increase leverage, the analyst believes that Viper has enough capacity for opportunistic buybacks.

    Sources indicate that bilkoski noted that Viper has historically delivered one of the highest production per share growth profiles in his royalty coverage, but still trades at a notable discount to the royalty peer average and the company's historical FCF yield range. "In our view, its above-average growth warrants a higher valuation," said the analyst.

    Sources indicate that bilkoski ranks No. 525 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.80%. See Viper Energy Stock Buybacks on TipRanks.

    Exxon Mobil (XOM) reported robust Q3 2026 profits, as its U.S. refineries boosted production to capitalize on the high diesel fuel prices sparked by the conflict in the Middle East. The oil and gas giant announced a quarterly dividend of $1.07 per share, payable on Dec. 10, reflecting a 3.9% increase. This marks Exxon's 44th consecutive year of dividend increases. At an annualized dividend of $4.28 per share, XOM offers a yield of 2.53%.

    Impressed by the Q3 print, TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Exxon stock and raised his price target to $193 from $180 to reflect higher downstream earnings, with the expectation of increased mid-cycle margins.

    Industry observers note that gabelman noted that the strength in Exxon's refining business continues to offset Middle East-related headwinds. He added that the company increased its ownership in LNG projects, which should reduce its Middle East concentration over time from 75% to 50% and lower the likelihood of diversification-focused mergers and acquisitions. Beyond LNG, Gabelman expects Exxon's growth in the 2030s to come from Guyana, Kashagan, Permian, and possibly Venezuela.

    Gabelman noted that Exxon declared a dividend hike of nearly 4% and aims to maintain buybacks at $20 billion for 2027. "The decision to maintain reduces the pro-cyclicality nature of the buyback," noted the analyst.

    Gabelman ranks No. 347 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 66% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.90%. See Exxon Mobil Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Williams (WMB), which owns and operates energy infrastructure to deliver natural gas, reported strong third-quarter results. The manufacturer announced a quarterly dividend of $0.525 per share, or $2.10 per share annualized, payable on Dec. 28. WMB offers a dividend yield of 3.09%.

    Industry observers note that in reaction to the Q3 2026 results, CIBC analyst Robert Catellier reaffirmed a buy rating on Williams stock with a price target of $82. The analyst noted that Q3 results were essentially in line with expectations and reflected continued strength in execution across WMB's infrastructure portfolio.

    Catellier said that Williams' Q3 performance was driven by higher transmission, storage, and power generation revenues, as well as contributions from the Momentum Midstream acquisition.

    He noted that Williams maintained its full-year EBITDA guidance of $8.3 billion to $8.5 billion. WMB continues to target long-term EBITDA compound annual growth rate of at least 11% through 2030.

    Catellier expects WMB's long-term targets to be supported by incremental transmission and storage opportunities, including Transco's Southeast Supply Enhancement II project and an 84 MMcf/d expansion of the Garden Connector project.

    Berkshire Hathaway’s CEO, Greg Abel, Just Bought $9.6 Billion Worth of 1 of Buffett’s Favorite Stocks

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (861 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 27, 2026 at 9:45AM EST.
    • 10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.
    • Greg Abel became the CEO of Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -0.04%) (BRKB +0.10%) at the beginning of this year after the conglomerate's longtime leader and legendary investor, Warren Buffett, stepped down.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 27, 2026 at 9:45AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.

    Greg Abel became the CEO of Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA -0.04%) (BRKB +0.10%) at the beginning of this year after the conglomerate's longtime leader and legendary investor, Warren Buffett, stepped down. Abel has had a busy first year in charge of the company, and many of his moves have been reminiscent of those his mentor would have made.

    Recent findings suggest that that's not surprising. Abel was quick to reassure investors that Berkshire Hathaway's values and culture wouldn't change under his leadership, and we have seen plenty of evidence that he meant those words. For instance, during the third quarter, Berkshire Hathaway spent $9.6 billion buying one of Buffett's favorite stocks. Here's what investors need to know.

    Greg Abel. Image source: Getty Images.

    It has been revealed that when people try to guess Buffett's favorite stock, Apple (AAPL +0.72%) is usually near the top of the list. That makes sense. Apple has been in Berkshire Hathaway's public equity portfolio since 2016; it has been the conglomerate's largest holding for years, and Buffett once remarked it is probably the best business in the world.

    Industry observers note that buffett has also praised Apple's now-former CEO, Tim Cook, on multiple occasions. However, there is one stock Berkshire Hathaway has spent even more on over the past decade or so: its own stock.

    Recent findings suggest that yes, Buffett loves Apple. But under his leadership, Berkshire Hathaway spent far more on share buybacks than it did on buying Apple shares over the past 10 years. That policy has continued under Greg Abel, who oversaw the conglomerate's $9.6 billion in buybacks during the third quarter.

    NYSE · As of 10:35 AM ET 11/27/26.

    In a recent development, like most corporate strategies, share buybacks aren't inherently good or bad. A lot depends on the details. But they do tend to signal management's confidence in the tech giant's outlook. Massive buybacks are a sign that a corporation's top executives believe shares are undervalued relative to the business's growth potential.

    Recent findings suggest that if that's really the case, then buybacks, by lowering the total number of outstanding shares, increase intrinsic value per share. Of course, the opposite is true if shares are actually overvalued. Where does Berkshire Hathaway stand right now? We can always trust Buffett and Abel's judgment. After all, Buffett crushed broader equities in his six-decade tenure as CEO of Berkshire Hathaway.

    Few people are more capable than he is at determining whether a company's shares are trading below their intrinsic value, particularly one he knows as deeply as the corporation he led for a long time. Abel is not Buffett, but he learned under the Oracle of Omaha's leadership, occupied high-level positions at Berkshire for a long time, and was handpicked to be Buffett's successor.

    Recent findings suggest that however, we don't have to put our blind faith in Buffett and Abel (although in this case, that faith would hardly be blind). We can look at how the business is doing ourselves. Now, Berkshire Hathaway is a complex conglomerate with multiple moving parts. But Buffett himself gave us a framework to approximate the manufacturer's intrinsic value in a 2018 letter to shareholders.

    He argued that Berkshire Hathaway can be separated into five "groves," each of which can be valued separately. We can then get close to the business' total value by adding up the individual groves' values, making the appropriate adjustments (taxes, debt, etc.), and dividing that total by the number of shares outstanding to get the intrinsic value per share. By my calculation, Berkshire Hathaway is currently slightly undervalued, by about 8% to 10%, although the answer can change depending on the earnings multiple we apply to certain parts of the business.

    According to recent reports, but if my answer is roughly in agreement with that of Abel and Buffett -- who know infinitely more about Berkshire Hathaway than I do -- then I am fine with that. There is another aspect to consider. Berkshire Hathaway is arguably an outstanding hedge against current market uncertainty. Some are worried about a shaky geopolitical and economic environment.

    According to recent reports, others worry that AI stocks are overvalued and will drag broader equities into a bear market. Berkshire Hathaway has a vast and diversified business with multiple parts that will respond differently to whatever troubles lie ahead. The tech giant also has some exposure to AI, though not too much, through its public equity portfolio, especially its stake in Alphabet (GOOG -0.48%) (GOOGL -0.37%). So, investors have a lot to gain by investing in the stock and holding onto it for a long time.

    10 stocks we like better than Simpson Manufacturing ›.

    Anthropic vs. SpaceX: Which Is the Better Giant IPO Buy?

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.
    • Industry observers note that the initial public offering (IPO) market has delivered two historic moments this year, and both involve the artificial intelligence (AI) boom.
    • But the celebration has faded quickly.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adria Cimino – Nov 27, 2026 at 10:05AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.

    Industry observers note that the initial public offering (IPO) market has delivered two historic moments this year, and both involve the artificial intelligence (AI) boom. Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +3.55%) listed on the Nasdaq in June in what was then the largest IPO ever, and Anthropic (ANT +8.52%), the manufacturer behind the Claude AI models, topped that record with its own debut on Nov. 19.

    But the celebration has faded quickly. SpaceX shares trade well below their first-day closing price, and Anthropic closed below its $83 IPO price on Tuesday, just four trading days after its debut. Investors are grappling with a familiar worry: Are these companies spending too much?

    It has been revealed that both companies are growing at breathtaking speeds, and both are spending enormous sums to keep up. So which of these latest giants is the better buy today? Let's find out.

    It has been revealed that anthropic's growth is hard to ignore. Earlier this decade, Dario Amodei and a small group of fellow researchers left OpenAI and released this rival AI lab. And in 2023, Anthropic launched its first Claude AI model. Since then, it's released new versions and has seen revenue soar.

    In a recent development, annual revenue climbed from $41 million in 2023 to $4.6 billion last year, and in the third quarter of this year, revenue topped $17 billion. Enterprise demand is driving this incredible momentum: More than 1,900 customers generated at least $1 million in revenue, and 250 customers were responsible for $10 million in revenue over the trailing 12 months.

    NASDAQ · As of 10:41 AM ET 11/27/26.

    The company faces a number of risks, however, including the investment needed to develop its models over time. Anthropic must generate a certain level of revenue to pay for the enormous amounts of compute required. The company's revenue is mainly consumption-based and not subject to long-term contractual commitments, yet its infrastructure commitments extend over many years. The risk is that revenue won't keep up with these spending commitments.

    In a recent development, spaceX's growth is just as impressive, and the firm has made significant progress on profitability. In the third quarter, SpaceX reported net income of more than $4 billion, compared to a year-earlier loss of more than $1 billion.

    The industrial and tech giant also has more than one engine, operating the Starlink connectivity business, the space business, and an AI segment. What's interesting here is that progress in reusable rockets may benefit all three businesses, as it ensures the manufacturer's ability to launch critical materials into space. For example, reusable rockets may transport Starlink's satellites. This is more cost-effective and could help SpaceX advance more quickly toward its goals.

    NASDAQ · As of 10:39 AM ET 11/27/26.

    It has been revealed that then there's the potential Tesla merger. Musk has said he's considering a combination, and special committees at both companies are weighing a reported all-stock deal, according to press reports. Musk sees synergies in AI, chips, robotics, and orbital computing, though a deal would also add complexity.

    Recent findings suggest that spending is the concern here, too, as SpaceX's capital spending far exceeds its revenue. In the third quarter, capex surpassed $19 billion while revenue came it a $14 billion. Investors will want to see returns on this investment.

    Both stocks could reward patient investors, but each is spending heavily on AI infrastructure and faces the risk that returns may arrive later than expected. Still, SpaceX looks like the better buy today.

    Anthropic is essentially a single bet on enterprise AI demand, and much of its revenue depends on usage that customers can scale back. SpaceX, meanwhile, has Starlink generating real operating income, a launch business, and a fast-growing AI arm, so profits from one area can help fund growth in another. It was also profitable in the third quarter.

    That said, a Tesla deal isn't guaranteed, and both stocks may stay volatile as the post-IPO dust settles.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.
    • Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively latest corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure.
    • It has been revealed that the growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

    Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively latest corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

    It has been revealed that the growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

    Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    Securitize reinforced "certain areas of the manufacturer like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo said. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

    In a recent development, securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The company posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

    Also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and announced the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

    Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo remarked.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

    "We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 27, 2026 at 10:11AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Celsius Holdings ›.

    Recent findings suggest that growth-oriented investors often debate between rapid expansion and established profitability. Choosing between Celsius (CELH +3.19%) and lululemon athletica (LULU +0.93%) requires weighing explosive functional beverage sales against steady athletic apparel dominance.

    Celsius focuses on the functional energy drink market, targeting health-conscious consumers with its proprietary formulas. lululemon athletica dominates the premium athletic apparel space with a loyal following. Both companies rely on strong brand identities to navigate the competitive consumer landscape, making them frequent candidates for long-term portfolios.

    Celsius develops and markets functional drinks that appeal to health-conscious consumers, a growing segment among beverage stocks. The manufacturer depends significantly on its partnership with Pepsi, which acts as the primary distributor for its products across the United States. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as Pepsi accounted for nearly 43.2% of total net revenue in its latest annual report.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $3.2 billion. This figure reflects a revenue growth rate of approximately 49.1% compared to the prior twelve-month period. Net income for this time frame was close to $317 million, resulting in a net margin of approximately 10% during this phase of aggressive expansion.

The debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.2x (0.22x), a metric that compares total debt against shareholder equity to evaluate financial leverage. In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $269.0 million, which is the cash remaining after paying for operating costs and equipment.

    lululemon athletica operates an omni-channel retail model that combines more than 800 company-operated stores with an expansive digital presence. The brand serves a global audience in 30 markets, offering technical athletic apparel and footwear designed for performance. By leveraging wholesale partnerships with fitness studios and international license arrangements, the company maintains a premium presence in the global apparel market.

    In the 12 months ended Aug. 2, 2026, revenue reached approximately $11.1 billion. This represents a revenue growth rate of nearly 1.7% over the previous twelve months. Net income during this timeframe was roughly $1.4 billion, yielding a net margin of close to 12.8% as the company focuses on balancing scale with profitability.

    According to recent reports, as of its February 2026 balance sheet, the current ratio is roughly 2.3x. The debt-to-equity ratio stands at approximately 0.4x, indicating the level of total debt used to finance company assets relative to shareholder equity. In the fiscal year ended Feb. 1, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $921.7 million, providing the company with substantial capital to reinvest in its global operations.

    Celsius faces significant concentration risks because a single distributor, Pepsi, accounts for a massive portion of its revenue and receivables. The organization must also defend its market share against large-scale competitors such as Monster Beverage (MNST -0.16%) and The Coca-Cola Company (KO -0.29%). Furthermore, the brand is vulnerable to potential regulatory actions regarding its health claims and must navigate supply chain complexities for materials like aluminum.

    It has been revealed that I'd go with Celsius. It has built a multi-brand energy drink company with PepsiCo's delivery network behind it, and it is profitable and just beginning to expand overseas. An exciting part of this business right now is Alani Nu, a real growth engine. Celsius bought the brand last year and now its top seller, with retail sales up about 50% year over year even without its record seasonal flavor, a hit that will be tough to repeat. Celsius does have things to work through, though. Its namesake brand is shrinking, higher aluminum and fuel costs are squeezing margins, and an investor lawsuit and a Texas investigation into how its drinks are marketed add uncertainty. Still, Alani Nu's growth lifted total sales 17%.

Its stock is cheaper than Celsius's relative to expected earnings, but it comes with a business that has yet to turn the corner.

    In a recent development, the players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

    Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

    But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

    The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

    The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

    There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

    Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

    In a recent development, sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

    It has been revealed that “He is a top player, no doubt about it,” said head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

    In a recent development, “He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”.

    A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

    Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

    Roberto De Zerbi has admitted that big-spending Tottenham Hotspur “are not a team yet” after watching his latest-look side fall to an opening-day defeat to Brentford.

    Tottenham have splashed out over £200m on latest players, but head coach De Zerbi has warned it will be impossible to set any targets until they become a team.

    Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow fresh signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

    Tottenham have been tipped to challenge for European qualification, having finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, but De Zerbi acknowledged those optimistic predictions may have come too soon.

    In a recent development, his team looked like strangers in their humiliating loss at Brentford and the Italian said: “We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target [for the season] when you become a team. Before you become a team, you can’t say what you can do.

    Recent findings suggest that “You can’t become a team from the transfer market on paper. You become a team when the players find a connection, a spirit, a soul.

    “We are not at the right point in our physical condition for a lot of reasons. Late from the World Cup and because in Australia [on pre-season], we don’t work in the right way. But no excuses, it’s a normal situation when you are building a new project. I don’t want time but we have to pass through these problems.

    It has been revealed that “I am surprised by the result and performance. They [Brentford] deserved to win and we played very bad. I knew we were not in the right condition. We can’t find an excuse. I am sorry for the result and performance.

    In a recent development, “Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali are not in the best physical condition. We knew that before the game. We have to improve on that and many other things, like organisation and pressing.

    According to recent reports, “We can improve rapidly but first, we have to understand this game better. I know their physical condition and [they are] new players but we have to put something more.

    “We had to fight more. Players know I have a lot of confidence in them and we hope to improve swiftly. Until we reach these conditions we have to suffer and today is an important defeat. Maybe we can wake up stronger.”.

By contrast, Igor Thiago, Kevin Schade and Dango Outtara scored 37 between them in the Premier League. Brentford are firm favourites with the bookies for this one, and that difference in firepower is probably why. Omar Marmoush could help matters.

    Seventeen-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett is one of the outstanding players in the country at his age group, and there is a lot of excitement about him at Spurs. Post-Kane, the club’s academy has not delivered much bona fide first-team quality, but Williams-Barnett appears on that trajectory.

    Brentford XI: Kelleher, Schade, Jensen, Thiago, Ouattara, Sangare, Ajer, Collins, Lewis-Potter, Janelt, Kayode.

    Subs: Valdimarsson, Hickey, Henry, Pinnock, Yarmoliuk, Wilson, Anthony, Damsgaard, Schuster.

    Your Bees to kick-off the 26/27 season 🐝 pic.twitter.com/nJO5emjgQM.

    Spurs XI: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Senesi, Robertson; Gallagher, Tonali, Bergvall; Moore, Richarlison, Tel.

    Subs: Dubravka, Danso, Maddison, Udogie, Fernandes, Solanke, Bentancur, Davies, Williams-Barnett.

    Our Spurs side on the opening day 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/Uh5z221aTc.

    Starting the season in west London 📌 pic.twitter.com/uglTu9zDvA.

    Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

    It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

    Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

    Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the big spenders.

    That is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s new leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

    The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

    Industry observers note that de Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

    Spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

    Sources indicate that brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

    Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the big boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

    Asked about the Mali international, Andrews remarked: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

    “He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”.

    Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

The insurer's book value per share has expanded by 83% since its initial public offering, indicating strong compounding power. Management continues to navigate shifting property rates by reallocating capital to casualty and specialty lines, where margins remain higher. Three things management said stand out.

    Hamilton Select, the company's excess and surplus lines unit that writes non-standard high-risk insurance, expanded 22% during the quarter. Proprietary artificial intelligence tools sort incoming submissions instantly, giving underwriters a speed advantage with wholesale broker partners.

    In a recent development, as Hamilton Insurance shifts toward longer-tail casualty lines, management extended fixed-income asset duration, the sensitivity of its bond portfolio to interest rate changes, to 3.8 years. Rising portfolio yields create a steady stream of investment income that supports overall profitability.

    Industry observers note that targeted growth in specialty reinsurance and lower-middle-market coverage provides a clear expansion runway. Long-standing distribution relationships and proprietary underwriting technology give the tech giant a distinct operational edge while management keeps a close eye on casualty loss cost trends.

    Disciplined capital allocation remains central to navigating changing market dynamics across property and casualty lines.
