    In a recent development, monday Night Fulham. ⚪️ pic.twitter.com/Oxuni9yiez.

    Two former Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain teammates go head-to-head in the dugouts at Craven Cottage as Fulham host Chelsea in a west London derby to round out the opening weekend of the latest Premier League season. Alvaro Arbeloa and Xabi Alonso were teammates at Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain and both had stints as Real Madrid manager last season but have new homes in London. Arbeloa has replaced Marco Silva, who is now at Benfica, whilst Alonso is Liam Rosenior’s permanent replacement. This is the first time a manager’s Premier League debut has come against someone he also played alongside in the competition.

    Sources indicate that “I know Alonso well because I have watched so many games of his teams,” Arbeloa mentioned. “We have to be ready, and if we want to beat them we will have to play very well. I spoke to Xabi a few days ago. But not about football; both of our families are coming to London, and we are very good friends, until Monday night [tonight]. We will be there on the touchline, so close for 90 minutes, and we will give everything for our clubs. For those 90 minutes, we are not friends.”.

    In a recent development, arbeloa has gone back to his former club to add a couple of players in the shape of Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios. The opening weekend has not served Fulham well of late; they have won just one of their last six Premier League opening weekend fixtures. They concluded their pre-season with a 1-0 win over Stuttgart.

    According to recent reports, chelsea have been very active in the transfer market this summer, breaking the British transfer record to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa as well as adding experience through the likes of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, whilst the likes of Marc Cucurella, Andrey Santos and Trevoh Chalobah have moved on. They finished off their pre-season with a 3-1 victory over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge just over a week ago.

    “We feel ready,” Alonso noted. “We have prepared the whole pre-season with some players from the first day, other ones coming later, but the desire, the ambition, the hunger to start the Premier League is already in the building each training [session] and we are looking forward to it.”.

    Enzo Fernandez has been strongly linked with a move away this summer, with Manchester City’s interest well-known.

    Recent findings suggest that “Enzo is a Chelsea player,” Alonso added. “He is a top, top player. He is training really well since he started 10 days ago with the team, very integrated. We are happy with him and he is getting ready for Monday. He is training really well, good attitude and that is what we want. He is trying his best to prepare for the kick-off of the Premier League.”.

    These sides finished on the same number of points (52) last season, with Chelsea finishing ahead on goal difference. It was one win apiece for each club in the two Premier League meetings last season. Nearly a year ago, Chelsea won 2-0 at Stamford Bridge whilst Fulham won 2-1 in this fixture at Craven Cottage back in January. Chelsea have won six of the past eight Premier League meetings at Craven Cottage.

    Planes, trains and automobiles: The best ways to beat travel fatigue—so you can come home feeling rested and fulfilled

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (502 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • All potentially exhausting options for the annual tradition of convening around the dinner table with loved ones on Thanksgiving.
    • It has been revealed that an estimated 81.5 million Americans are projected to travel, or have already traveled, at least 50 miles from their homes between Nov.
    • Industry observers note that high gas prices and soaring plane ticket costs may factor into the shift.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Five-hour flights. Eleven-hour road trips. Fifteen-hour train rides. All potentially exhausting options for the annual tradition of convening around the dinner table with loved ones on Thanksgiving.

    It has been revealed that an estimated 81.5 million Americans are projected to travel, or have already traveled, at least 50 miles from their homes between Nov. 24 and Nov. 30, according to the American Automobile Association. And their mode of transportation is shifting: Fewer people are flying or driving this year compared to 2025, and more are traveling by buses, trains and cruises, AAA data shows.

    Industry observers note that high gas prices and soaring plane ticket costs may factor into the shift. As of Wednesday evening, fuel prices are roughly 17% higher than they were on the same date in 2025, according to AAA data. Meanwhile, "months of elevated jet fuel costs due to the conflict in Iran have contributed to Thanksgiving and Christmas airfares reaching 10-year highs," according to fare-tracking platform Hopper.

    The alternate modes of transit may open travelers up to fresh experiences — and new forms of travel fatigue to keep you from returning home feeling rested and fulfilled. You're probably already familiar with the exhaustion you might get from a day of plane travel, for example. In airplanes, "there can be lower humidity, maybe lower oxygen levels at cabin pressure. Sometimes people report feeling more dehydrated or drained. You're adjusting to that change in altitude," says Alaina Tiani, a Cleveland Clinic behavioral sleep medicine psychologist.

    Sources indicate that but even waiting in places like train stations or cruise ports can feel draining due to sheer sensory overload, Tiani indicates. And then, depending on your mode of travel, you may still need to deal with cramped seating and limited ability to get up and walk around or drink some water and eat a snack.

    Industry observers note that once you arrive at your destination, managing responsibilities like remembering where you put your hotel key and deciding what to eat and how to structure your day can also take a mental toll, says travel writer Shannon O'Donnell, who's written about managing travel fatigue. "All of that actually requires a lot more thinking and planning for your brain," she says, adding: "People just don't understand how those add up and why a relaxing vacation suddenly has them feeling wrecked.".

    Sources indicate that the consequences can sneak up on you, O'Donnell notes. Travel fatigue can "present as maybe a lack of interest in something that you might usually find fascinating," she says. Instead of looking out the window on a plane ride or playing car games with your kids on a road trip, you might disengage and appear apathetic to the people around you.

    You might stand a better chance of a fulfilling, restful holiday if you prepare for your travel fatigue. Here, Tiani and O'Donnell share their advice for how to do it:.

    #155017. Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (745 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (745 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S.
    • The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.
    • Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S. history — delivered a major win for the company and its investors. But it failed at another task: reviving animal spirits in the AI trade.

    The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.

    It wasn't supposed to play out this way.

    Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.

    It has been revealed that some of those worries resurfaced Thursday as a short seller, Hunterbrook Media, alleged in a report that firmware sold by chipmaker AMD had turned up in U.S.-blacklisted companies. AMD stock closed down more than 7%. The chipmaker told CNBC it complies with U.S. law.

    Industry observers note that adding to the worries, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released documents showing that a subagency of the Commerce Department approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. That also raised the prospect of an Asia sales slowdown under stricter export controls.

    Many investors and analysts continue to express confidence in the AI trade, noting that Anthropic's successful market debut — the stock closed up 17% from its IPO price and raised more than $81 billion — bodes well for capital spending across tech.

    But investors acknowledged that this is a high-tension moment and mentioned it's time to be more strategic about the trade.

    Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, described himself as a "circumspect bull," making the comparison to market conditions in 2022 when the big indices tanked in the back half of the year.

    "You could have still made money that year. You just needed to have the right combination of longs and shorts," he stated.

    It has been revealed that part of the challenge, Niles said, has been a price war between the two cutting-edge frontier labs, Anthropic and OpenAI. That has posed a threat to the overall revenue and profit potential of AI and the capex going into it. Fierce competition on price is producing collective losses between the two top companies, he notes.

    "The combined revenue growth for OpenAI plus Anthropic went from growing 75% sequentially in Q2 to 48% in Q3," he told CNBC. "The combined losses went from $7.9 billion to about $8.4 billion from Q2 to Q3.".

    While uncertainty is high now, some resolution may be on the horizon if a greater degree of commercial and regulatory clarity emerges over the next few months.

    Trading experts also told CNBC that the tech sector's troubles Thursday were a more serious matter than Anthropic simply siphoning capital from other parts of the market.

    "There's a reset of AI in general," said JJ Kinahan, senior vice president at Cboe Global Markets.

    Investors for years have profited in tech by buying the dip, he mentioned, but "there's been an attitude change that [you] can't buy things blindly and they'll all go up." Nvidia's ongoing declines have shaken confidence in the buy-the-dip strategy, he said.

    Anthropic's next few trading days will be a key gauge of the market's strength. Friday will be a "wild card," Kinahan stated. It could be a "final flush out" for the market, or a bounce that leaves the market in "no man's land" while volatility remains elevated.

    A better gauge may be Monday, when options on Anthropic start trading, providing insight into whether retail investors will back the organization in force — providing more of a vote of confidence in the AI trade.

    "If people think we're going up [on Anthropic] they'll buy stock, but retail particularly will just buy calls," he stated. "There's a bigger test coming Monday.".

    For now, investors continue to sell AI-related stocks.

    Neoclouds, the generally highly indebted AI-dedicated computing providers at the outer edges of the AI trade, were down substantially Thursday, with CoreWeave closing down more than 6%.

    Hyperscalers such as Alphabet and Amazon.com, viewed as relatively defensive AI bets, also finished lower.

    One bright spot: Cybersecurity stocks continued to rally, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike both closing up. AI is finding security holes across software infrastructure, creating a scramble to patch the vulnerabilities before hackers can exploit them.

    — CNBC's Daren Fonda contributed reporting.

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (473 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    What is ‘texture-maxxing’? The food trend putting crunch on the menu

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (473 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Texture-maxxing is the latest food trend taking social media by storm as consumers, driven by aesthetics and taste, look for a sensory experience.
    • It has been revealed that british supermarket Waitrose's latest food and drink report highlighted "texture-maxxing" as one of the trends of the year.
    • It has been revealed that "This year, the sound of food went mainstream," Waitrose's Senior Development Chef Will Torrent said in the Wednesday report.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Texture-maxxing is the latest food trend taking social media by storm as consumers, driven by aesthetics and taste, look for a sensory experience.

    It has been revealed that british supermarket Waitrose's latest food and drink report highlighted "texture-maxxing" as one of the trends of the year. It describes the phenomenon as a multi-sensory indulgence that is "fuelled by texture-maxxing crunch and intense flavour hits," pushing shoppers to fill their trolleys with crunchy peanut butter, dumplings, and trifles.

    It has been revealed that "This year, the sound of food went mainstream," Waitrose's Senior Development Chef Will Torrent said in the Wednesday report. "Driven by social media's obsession with audible, multi-sensory cooking, we're creating high-contrast meals that combine shatter-crisp crunch with pillowy chew.".

    "The emphasis in social media content has flipped from narrative voiceovers to ASMR-inspired audio, where the evocative sounds of food are just as vital as the visuals," he added.

    In a recent development, food trends on social media have ranged from the obvious to the absurd. Fibermaxxing and proteinmaxxing have taken off in the past few years. Meanwhile, food and beverages like Dubai chocolate, protein coffee, and ube were some of the big social media hits.

    Nestlé's USA 2026 trends found that 75% of Gen Z and 80% of millennials sought out texture in snack cravings with the hashtag "crunchtok," amassing 1.5 billion views.

    Waitrose noted that shoppers looking to maximize on texture bought its viral No.1 Alphonso Mango Dessert, which involves "cracking through the crisp shell" to access a "smooth mango mousse and passion fruit curd on a crunchy white chocolate base.".

    Waitrose's TikTok and Instagram videos of eating the dessert were watched by more than two million people, with a whopping 6,173 hours and 36 minutes of play time on TikTok. Its videos featuring crunchy toast also went viral.

    The U.K. grocer's sales of jarred chili crunches, which include crispy rayu oils such as itsu Crispy Chilli Oil, saw a 13-fold jump. Meanwhile, crunchy peanut butter outsold smooth.

    Dumplings also had a moment, with sales of chicken gyoza dumplings up 116% this year and searches on waitrose.com for gochujang and peanut butter udon noodles jumped 60%.

    "We've seen an explosion in demand as shoppers treat dumplings not just as a quick weeknight bite, but as a total sensory experience," Waitrose's Executive Chef Stephen Parkins-Knight said.

    "Driven by the rise of texture-maxxing, people want that ultimate contrast: delicate skins, juicy fillings and crispy skirts, topped with very chilli crunch. With innovation ranging from fusion fillings to rich dipping broths, dumplings have taken a delicious centre stage in 2026," he added.

    Texture-maxxing also extended to desserts, as shoppers bought twice as many chocolate trifles compared to 2025, and sales of strawberry trifles increased 160%.

    Tiramisu was also popular, with searches for waitrose.com's tiramisu recipe page increasing 155% year-on-year.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.

    Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence company in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.

    Sources indicate that "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday. "It's our best performing equity by far in ARKVX, our venture fund. ... Our confidence has grown with time as it really took over the enterprise" AI business.

    Anthropic shares jumped 17% in their first day, but closed well off the highs of the session and were headed for sizable losses Friday. The Nasdaq, which was expected to get a boost from a major IPO reviving enthusiasm about the technology trade, fell by 2% on Thursday.

    In a recent development, "We're climbing a wall of worry," said Wood. "Everybody is worried about AI hype and the political situation after the election, but I think we'll look back and say, OK this is more like the '80s and '90s, climbing a wall of worry you know with bricks much like what we have today: inflation, interest rates, wars, latest technologies and so forth so quite optimistic here.".

    In a recent development, the Anthropic stakes are relatively small across the funds, but Wood typically will buy shares in companies she likes steadily during long stretches. Wood said she is "averaging down" with her purchases of Anthropic.

    In a recent development, in her $6.1 billion Ark Innovation ETF, Anthropic is a 0.3% stake. The biggest holdings in that fund are Tesla and SpaceX, representing more than 21% of the fund together.

    Recent findings suggest that ark Innovation, which retail investors piled into during the pandemic as it gained about 150% in 2020, tumbled the subsequent next two years, losing 67% in 2022 alone. Wood's following was dented after the substantial losses.

    The fund had a comeback stretch as the bull market revved back up from 2023 to 2025, but has fallen on hard times again this year, down more than 10% in 2026. The S&P 500 is up 4.8% this year.

    Wood dismissed comparisons of today's environment to the dot-com bubble.

    Recent findings suggest that "Back then if an Anthropic had gone public, it probably would have gone up threefold the first day," she said. "That's how crazy things were.".

    • Two Italians have been killed after an alleged Iranian attack on Kuwait, Kuwaiti forces noted Thursday.
    • In a post on X, Kuwait's army said the deaths followed Iranian attacks on the country, with the two Italians killed by falling missile debris.
    • Industry observers note that in response, a spokesperson for Iran's military told state media that no offensive or military operations had been carried out in the area and that "these accusations should be viewed as a cover for continued malevolence and an attempt to exacerbate insecurity in the region" by U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Two Italians have been killed after an alleged Iranian attack on Kuwait, Kuwaiti forces noted Thursday.

    In a post on X, Kuwait's army said the deaths followed Iranian attacks on the country, with the two Italians killed by falling missile debris. Two others were also injured.

    Industry observers note that in response, a spokesperson for Iran's military told state media that no offensive or military operations had been carried out in the area and that "these accusations should be viewed as a cover for continued malevolence and an attempt to exacerbate insecurity in the region" by U.S. and Israeli forces.

    Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi noted on Telegram that he had spoken with his Italian counterpart, Antonio Tajani, and expressed regret over their deaths, while stressing that Tehran had no role or involvement in the incident.

    "The incident is suspicious and looks like a precooked recipe for war," Araghchi wrote on X.

    He also said Iran was ready to cooperate with the governments of Kuwait and Italy in investigating the incident.

    Industry observers note that separately, Israel said Thursday that it was prepared to carry out strikes against Iran "at any moment," even without U.S. forces joining the effort, according to Israeli military spokesman Effie Defrin on Israeli broadcaster Kan.

    According to recent reports, the comments came after U.S. envoy Jared Kushner told a podcast Wednesday that Israel "needs to get out of the constant wartime mindset.".

    Israel has been pushing the Trump administration to back another offensive against Tehran, with Reuters reporting on Nov. 18 that Israeli spy chief Roman Gofman pushed for joint strikes when he met U.S. officials earlier in the month.

    Late Thursday, President Donald Trump noted on PBS that the U.S. had "victory at hand" in the Iran conflict and reiterated that victory would come "whenever I want it to be, to be honest.".

    According to recent reports, speaking during a Thanksgiving call with U.S. military personnel, Trump remarked Washington was still trying to give Iran "every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives.".

    But he added that he was not sure whether Tehran would agree.

    "Some people question why. Are they crazy? Maybe they are," Trump stated.

    #154995. It’s not just you: Durable goods are getting less reliable, from sputtering cars to glitching smart TVs

    📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (776 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    It’s not just you: Durable goods are getting less reliable, from sputtering cars to glitching smart TVs

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (776 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • "They just don't make things like they used to." The phrase, formerly exclusive to grandparents, is now used by consumers of all ages.
    • In a recent development, across the United States, durable goods like cars, appliances and electronics are becoming less reliable.
    • Consumers have noticed: Shoppers dealing with high inflation rates and added tariffs on imported goods are unsatisfied with all kinds of products, from cars and tech devices to furniture and kitchen gear.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    "They just don't make things like they used to." The phrase, formerly exclusive to grandparents, is now used by consumers of all ages.

    In a recent development, across the United States, durable goods like cars, appliances and electronics are becoming less reliable. In the automobile industry, owners of 3-year-old models reported an average of 204 problems per 100 vehicles as of Feb. 12, the highest level since 2022, according to a report from consumer intelligence company J.D. Power. Reliability is a growing concern for dishwashers and front-load washers too, respectively experiencing an average of 92 and 91 problems per 100 units as of Oct. 29, according to a similar J.D. Power report.

    Consumers have noticed: Shoppers dealing with high inflation rates and added tariffs on imported goods are unsatisfied with all kinds of products, from cars and tech devices to furniture and kitchen gear. Just over three-quarters of Americans say they believe companies often sell lower-quality products and services at higher prices, according to an Axios and Harris Poll survey published in May 2025.

    It has been revealed that to be sure, reliability and durability aren't the only ways to define a product's quality. Aesthetics and performance matter to consumers, too. Your television today may not last as long as the one you grew up with, but it's probably larger and thinner with better picture definition — and it likely costs much less, when adjusted for inflation, says Justin Sirotin, an industrial design professor at the Rhode Island School of Design. Indeed, the average price of a television was roughly $622 in 1996 adjusted for inflation, whereas a 55-inch LCD model now costs $232 on average.

    But because they're penny-pinched, consumers are becoming more focused on finding high-value products — ones that perform consistently and reliably — than on price, according to a 2025 Deloitte report.

    In a recent development, unfortunately for shoppers, some businesses are also economically squeezed, and may manufacture products with cheaper, less durable parts to keep their profits growing, Sirotin claims. Plus, we've all gotten used to sleek products with impressive features at affordable prices, and when businesses have to deliver on those aspects to grow demand, longevity can drop down the list of priorities. Manufacturers may prioritize quality on the external parts of a product — like the picture quality on a television — and get their cost savings with cheaper internal components that you won't initially notice, says Keyana Sapp, an investigative journalist and creator of the Worse on Purpose newsletter.

    In some cases, a product's durability may even be part of a "planned obsolescence," wherein businesses intentionally give goods a certain lifespan so customers need to buy replacements within a predictable timeframe. Planned obsolescence isn't necessarily rampant, and it's hard to prove that any individual company purposefully designs products to fail, Sapp indicates.

    But historically speaking, it's not entirely a conspiracy theory. In 1924, major light bulb manufacturers formed an international coalition and agreed to lower and standardize the lifespan of incandescent light bulbs to 1,000 hours. The cartel broke up during World War II.

    According to recent reports, you can, of course, try extending the longevity of products you've already bought by paying to repair them, rather than getting a brand-upcoming replacement. But as devices like vacuum cleaners and headphones evolve technologically, they require increasingly specialized tools and labor, claims Shahram Mokhtari, lead teardown technician at online repair community and e-commerce site iFixit. Specialized screws, glued components and limited access to repair information can make some products difficult or impossible to fix, the Federal Trade Commission reported in May 2021.

    Europe has right-to-repair regulations that require manufacturers of certain products to provide access to replacement parts, tools and information. Only nine U.S. states have similar legislation for consumer electronics.

    If you want to know how long a product might last before you buy it, look up its reviews or do some research to understand if it's complicated to fix, Mokhtari recommends. Or, if you have the budget, you can prioritize higher-priced products that might bring both initial quality and long-term longevity. This may require intentional long-term planning for some consumers — even as online shopping has made impulse buying easier, Sirotin notes.

    In a recent development, "It takes a lot of intentionality by the consumer to say, 'OK, well, is this chair really a chair that I want to have for 25 years? Or is this the chair I'm going to buy and sit in for six months, and then I'm just going to get another chair?'" claims Sirotin.

    #154993. Latest Update: Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

    📅 25 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 21m • 📚 Deep Dive (4173 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

    📅 25 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4173 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.
    • Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.
    • The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

    Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

    The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

    “England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his new club.

    Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

    Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h.

    Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

    “I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

    “He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”.

    Sources indicate that forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

    Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

    According to recent reports, forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a fresh right wing-back before the deadline.

    It has been revealed that newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

    It has been revealed that glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

    Recent findings suggest that “For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

    “We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”.

    This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

    Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

    According to recent reports, the most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

    It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

    Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

    “Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

    Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

    Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

    Ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp.

    You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

    Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

    Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

    It has been revealed that the 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

    Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a fresh forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

    Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

    According to recent reports, speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon said: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”.

    Recent findings suggest that of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”.

    "There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2.

    "It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C.

    A tough night for the home teams...

    Cardiff City 1 Norwich 2Doncaster Rovers 1 Middlesbrough 3Barnsley 3 Crewe Alexandra 2Blackburn Rovers 1 Sheffield United 2Blackpool 1 Lincoln City 4Cambridge United 0 Millwall 1Fleetwood Town 4 Shrewsbury Town 0Ipswich Town 3 Leicester City 1Plymouth 2 Coventry City 4Sheffield Wednesday 0 Wolverhampton Wanderers 2Southampton 1 West Ham United 4Stevenage Town 0 Reading 3Stoke City 1 Hull City 1 (4-5 pens)Walsall 0 Leyton Orient 0 (5-6 pens)Watford 1 Peterborough United 5Birmingham City 1 Brentford 6Nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2.

    According to recent reports, and that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

    It has been revealed that A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

    A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

    Sources indicate that there is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

    Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

    There will be six minutes of added time.

    Sources indicate that that just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

    Recent findings suggest that calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

    Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

    There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

    In a recent development, the “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

    According to recent reports, nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu launches a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

    Industry observers note that it's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP.

    Industry observers note that jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

    The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

    Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

    Stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

    Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

    He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

    There’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s new-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

    The substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

    Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

    Okafor demonstrates off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

    Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

    Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

    It has been revealed that end-to-end football! ⚡️First Wood, then Okafor - just 19 seconds between the two chances 😮#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/TGQmtwLNwE.

    Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”.

    This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

    Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

    Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm.

    It has been revealed that nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

    James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

    Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

    A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

    Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

    This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

    According to recent reports, both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

    James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

    Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

    In a recent development, should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

    Leeds have only won four from 10.

    What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ.

    It has been revealed that james wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

    Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

    And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

    Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

    Recent findings suggest that ampadu comes over to the left to fire in a long throw-in. Sels comes steaming out of his goal and fumbles the ball but is awarded a free-kick after Muharemovic makes contact. Looked very minimal in all fairness.

    Industry observers note that oof, a good chance for Aina! Williams’ cross from the left comes all the way through to his opposite wing-back, but Aina’s half-volley sails over. A cracking contact, though.

    Elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

    Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

    Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

    Recent findings suggest that what a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

    Industry observers note that nmecha attempts to break beyond the halfway line but is stymied by a swarm of Forest players. He demands a foul from the referee who is not interested in the least.

    It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

    Sources indicate that tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

    In a recent development, tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

    Industry observers note that the game has reached something of a holding pattern as both sides resolve to slow things down, at least temporarily. Forest have settled into a slightly deeper block.

    Sensing an opportunity, Ampadu spins in a glorious through-ball between centre-back and full-back for James to gallop on to. He hits the by-line and cuts back to Longstaff, but the midfielder can’t beat Sels. A good chance that probably should have been converted.

    A good chance goes begging! 🫣Longstaff is free for Leeds but fires it straight at Sels...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/0UJdfSDQ6w.

    Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

    In a recent development, both sides have physical, quick out-balls, which has made for a frenetic encounter thus far. James rasps in another fierce cross from the right after another sweeping Leeds move, but Nmecha cannot get there and Tanaka fires well over on the follow-up.

    Aina’s throw-in, this time from the left, is flicked on to Jesus at the back post and while the forward is able to direct the ball goalwards there is Justin on the line to clear the ball to safety.

    It has been revealed that chance! Dominguez slides in Aina down the right channel and the full-back’s mishit cross has Trafford scrambling. He palms the ball behind for a corner, which is headed away for a Forest throw-in on the far side.

    Leeds are enjoying a spell of possession here, Tanaka and Longstaff peeling off into the wide areas to collect the ball and disrupt Forest’s mid-block out-of-possession structure. The hosts are more than happy for Leeds to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure as, for the second time tonight, Trafford boots it out into touch.

    Sources indicate that dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

    Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

    Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

    James shows off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

    Sels goes long to Wood (feels like the right play given his attributes), James lands on the second ball but can only boot the ball into row Z to jeers from the home fans.

    Aina releases a long throw-in from the right and it’s headed behind for a corner. Trafford punches the inswinging delivery away and Williams’ effort from the edge of the box sails well over.

    Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

    Players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

    The first pre-match question put to Glasner by ITV was in relation to the reported £45m club-record deal for Chelsea forward Liam Delap. He responded: “I can tell everybody that he doesn’t play today. Everything else we shall see in the next days.”.

    Oliver Glasner breaks his silence on Nottingham Forest's record signing, Liam Delap 🚨He speaks to @gabrielclarke05 ahead of Forest's Carabao Cup tie against Leeds 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/8DlWMIzVS9.

    Reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

    “I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

    “We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”.

    Industry observers note that previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke remarked: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game. Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”.

    In a recent development, when asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a significant believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”.

    The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

    🏆x4⃣ pic.twitter.com/DRPXFa2kM3.

    This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

    Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

    Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

    Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

    Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

    Nottingham Forest Sels; Diomande, Jair, Milenkovic; Aina, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams; Jesus, Kalimuendo; Wood.

    Subs Victor, Murillo, Abbott, Netz, Hutchinson, Ndoye, McAtee, Sangare, Hudson Odoi.

    Leeds United Trafford; Rodon, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Ampadu, Tanaka, Longstaff, Justin; James, Okafor; Nmecha.

    Subs Perri, Lienou, Bijol, Bogle, Wilson, Cresswell, Stach, Aaronson, Calvert-Lewin.

    The massive breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

    Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

    It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

    Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a upcoming centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

    Farke makes six changes to the complement that started against Forest in the league on Saturday.

    According to recent reports, 📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/XuUzwwkmfi.

    Wood makes Glasner’s XI while summer acquisitions Diomande and Schlager are handed their first competitive Forest starts.

    Our @Carabao_Cup XI this evening. 📋 pic.twitter.com/Wv918WJScj.

    According to recent reports, welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s upcoming head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

    The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

    According to recent reports, daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.
